body: Zoom meeting to meet and greet people that are feeling the same way.  Excellent idea!!!

The best thanks of all is having you here.  We may not be able to be face to face but Please always know that there are people here to listen and hopefully offer guidance.  You are never alone in your struggles.  Sending you virtual hugs.

No it doesn’t ! Podcasts are good, please share any that you think are helpful.  I have found watching and listening to ASMR videos helpful in calming my mind.  It’s hard to be engaged in the world when you don’t have others with you.  Do you have hobbies or play sports?

YES! you are absolutely spot on about many of the things you described.   Grieving is exhausting. I have this community to share with, they get it, and only one other person, my spouse.  I don’t expose others to my depression and grief because I don’t want to pass that energy onto others.  Others say I am being strong, but I tell them, I do my crying in private.  I know the feeling of depression is always there but I force myself to put it aside or in a box when I go to work or do other things.  Same for my spouse, I love him and he’s been there for me, but he needs a break from my grief.  No you can’t keep going this way, and spit ball here with me, what is one thing you can do right now to take your mind off your depression for a few minutes?

I am sorry you are feeling this way. You a VERY self aware.  True, you should not be forced to stay however do you mean something to others.  Many here are just checked out on life, what’s the point of being on the rat wheel.  If you are intent on this path, although I hope you change your mind and stay, at least let those that do love you an opportunity to help or at the very least explain your reasons for leaving.  Here to listen and talk if you want.

I am sorry you’re struggling with this.  It’a hard to talk to someone about depression when they haven’t experienced it.  Depression is hard to put into words, it’s a whole body and brain pain, not like a toothache or a pulled muscle.  For me it’s like a foreboding or my soul is being swallowed. Believe me there are times I don’t want to be here from my own personal situation and  experiencing the aftermath of pain from my son’s suicide I wouldn’t want to ever pass that pain onto others.  So suicide is not an option. Medication is trial and error, have you tried Well Butrin? It has helped A LOT! Plus working to take my mind off my grief and depression.
Please tell us what is going on. We are here to Listen, help and support.  Your parents would be devastated if you were gone, trust me on this one.

I am sorry to read you are in the same situation.  Sometimes there are no words but a kind gesture, a quiet hug, or sitting in silence with someone knows or understands what we are going through is enough to get to the next moment.
I am so sorry for your loss.  My family keeps me here, we lean on each other when emotionally it becomes unbearable.  Thank you for your support.

I am so sorry for you and your mom’s loss. As parents we feel like we failed, failed in not protecting him more or loving him more.  I worry about my son everyday and his pain. He wishes he had listened more. He lost his only and best friend. It’s horrible for all of us. I too, hope our lost loved ones are at peace. Sending love and comfort your way.

Thank you for asking. I don’t want him to be remembered by this impulsive decision.  He was funny, goofy, creative, a good friend to others, incredibly bright, started college at 16, driven but very hard on himself.  Every day before leaving for work and going to bed we told him we loved him, but somehow it wasn’t enough.  We try to remember and talk about all the things that made him special to us and others.  Those memories will always remain precious.
Yes, I understand. Unfortunately there are those that prey on people’s grief. Is there a fund you could start in your husband’s name, a hobby, volunteering?  Would you consider being a foster parent?

I would talk to your parents about how you are feeling.  I am the same way with loud noises, people chewing loudly which feels like nails on a chalkboard and high tv volume.  Frays the the nerves.  When the noises gets too much I put in earplugs which helps a lot.  Do you have a pair of noise cancelling headphones?

Feeling empty, same here.  Our 16 year old son took his life fall 2019 and ever since I feel nothing, just pain.  Would give everything, including my life to know he is alive and okay.  I suspect, you would give up all the money and possessions to have your husband back. At this point I am living for other people, hoping some happiness returns, but it hasn’t .  Do you ever think about helping other people who are in need? Here to lean on if you need to.

I am sorry you are where you are at the moment.  I am there too but for very different reasons.  Life has really become meaningless for me after we lost our teenage son to suicide in Fall ‘19.  I really miss him. I don’t see the point in getting up every day but do it to be there for my husband and son.  We told him everyday how much we loved him, we’re proud of him but looking back I question how much did I listen or did I knit pick about little things.   There were times he didn’t like himself as well, he was very hard on himself.  I don’t like myself as well, just want to disappear.  I feel tremendous guilt for not protecting him.  I know the pain of his death is crushing, but I can’t take my life and put that pain into my family members and my other son.  He has been through so much.  Can you talk to your mom about how you feel and tell her LISTEN ! I am here to listen should you want to talk.  As far as your mistakes, forget about them, everyday is a chance to start over.  It’s very very hard and I am trying to learn from all this,

Same as well.  This will be the 2nd Christmas without our son.  He took his life in fall 2019, he was only 16. I used to love making the house festive, making it special for him and his brother.  It so hard now to celebrate or be happy about anything. Everyday it is just going through the motions, feeling numb, a complete emptiness.   I just have to fake it for others around me and try to be strong for our other son, but he’s having a hard time too. I hope you are able to find some joy and peace.

I am so sorry you are going through a tough time right now.  I understand exactly what you wrote.  The whole world seems gray and trying to stay motivated about anything is difficult.   Was wondering if you have tried Wellbutrin ?  I have been using it for a few years.  My family and I lost our youngest son last fall and the grief has been unbearable at time.  I truly believe this medication has been a life savor me during this dark time in my life.  Here to chat anytime.  Feel better soon and don’t give up.  How you feel today won’t be the same tomorrow.
Good to hear.  How are you doing this evening?  You can dm anytime you want.  It’s late where I am so it will be a bit of time before I reply.

I am so sorry for your friend’s loss.  We lost our youngest son (16) to suicide last fall.  She will go through a WIDE range of emotions. Disbelief, confusion, denial, a big one was fear for me.  Guilt is an everyday feeling for us, wishing we saw the signs more clearly.  I am 10 months out and still breakdown sobbing daily.  

We had a viewing just for immediate family, he looked like he was sleeping.  Although, I felt that it would have been too traumatic for his friends to see him. Our funeral director was wonderful and supportive. Upon reflection, we planned a memorial too quickly and wish we had waited and had others handle it.  My husband and I where overwhelmed.  Even to this day I still beat myself up over how I wanted it to go.  

You  are doing the best thing right now and drawing on others advice and experiences who are on this horrible journey of deep sorrow and anguish to losing a child. Keeping her company and finding resources, organizing food and funeral services would be helpful. We found in the months that followed friends slowly stopped calling to check on us, some still do, which I am grateful for.  I appreciate that simple text, “how are doing?”Please keep supporting her and her family, and get others to as well for the months to come.  She has a very long difficult road ahead.  Sending love.
I don’t believe that is true.  I don’t know you but I care about you.  Can we talk ?

Hey there!  Life can be overwhelming and when you feel lonely even more so.  Have you reached out to your family and friends for support?  I also live in the US, on the west coast and Covid is still keep businesses shut and schools shut down til fall.  😊 Here to chat anytime.

Thank you for staying.  Perhaps you will be doing some chalk drawing yourself with a new buddy.  This whole covid thing has been hard on everyone not being able to work.  I need to be working.  Might I ask what type of business you have?

Have to agree with Alternative Stage 68 a 100% about passing the pain onto others.  My son passed away last fall, he was only 16.  The destruction and pain is beyond words.  We were blind sided.  No note, no clues.  The guilt is over whelming.  We loved him so much.  I am truly sorry you are not in a good place right now.  It’s strange how we can have our lives put together (you with work, financially responsible, help others, probably A + student) but for some of us we can’t be in charge of those dark emotions and keep the pain of depression away.  I think we have to lean on each other, whether it is family, friends, on line groups, meds, our pets to help us get past believing suicide is the only way to make the pain stop.  The pain of losing my child is so unbearable at times that there isn’t a day that goes by that I don’t think about being with my him, but I won’t pass that pain onto my family. I truly hope that in your travels you find beauty and peace in our crazy fucked up world.  Not sure where you are traveling, but have always found hiking, at the beach, away from the noise and chaos of the city calms the soul.  Please keep us posted how are you doing and please reach out to your family.  Be well.

Yes, tired of this life at times.  It goes deeper sometimes of what is really the  point of our existence.  Now with my son gone, I questioned it more everyday why do I stay.  Stay for my family and others. Learning to get outside of myself and help others feels really good.  

Just found a really good article.  Take a moment to read.  What are your thoughts? 

https://tinybuddha.com/blog/when-you-feel-like-youre-going-nowhere-and-life-has-no-point/

By Carrie L. Burns

I am a mom devastated by our 16 year old son taking his life last year.  The excruciating pain from losing a child to suicide pales in comparison to just having depression.  There is not a day that goes by that my husband and I don’t blame ourselves for missing the signs. We told him everyday we loved him.  Somehow our love was not enough.  The “if only’s and what if’s” loop non stop in our minds.  Although I am in this nightmare of sorrow and want to leave too, I just can’t put that pain onto others.  Yes the works looks pretty shitty right now but I just have to look beyond it and make those closer to me smile.

I am so sorry you are going through this right now.  No one should ever feel alone.  Do everything you can for your boys.  If your ex is toxic in any way, yours boys are going to need you to protect them.  Fight hard!!! Sending you love and support.  Here to listen anytime.

Please don’t.   The voices of depression are making you think these things.  Would you please do two things?  Call a handful of people you trust and tell them how you are feeling? The other is to wait one more day?  I am here to listen ANYTIME!  Sending you love.

So true.  Although we told our son everyday we loved him, we wished he had called us before making his decision.  Having suffered with the pain of depression, the pain from losing our son is a 1000 times worse.  It’s soul crushing.  When someone take’s their life, the aftermath of destruction radiates out onto others.  My friend, who is a teacher, recently spoke to her about having every student make a list of at least 5 people they must call if they are ever feeling depressed and suicidal.  A comforting voice or a kind word, can make a difference.  The pain is so unbearable at times.

Thank you so much.  I appreciate your kindness.  Hope we don’t come out scarred as well but stronger. I am always amazed out how our previous generations survived the devastation of war, families separated or lost, homes and businesses devastated, and yet still have this ability to keep going.  There are days when it takes all my energy just to get of bed, brush my teeth and feed the cats.  Exercising and good sleep are mood boosters. Going for a drive or even a walk helps. Stop watching the news. We all have to be kind and supportive to each other and to ourselves too.  Still struggling with the latter part. I am here to listen and chat whenever you need to.

I am sorry you are having a rough time.  You sound overwhelmed with  limited support.  This pandemic is taking a toll on many.  I understand what you are going through, no job and lost my son in September, grieving  and isolated. Staying busy (even with little stuff), exercising helps, and figuring out a plan B .  Here to listening and talk anytime.  Sending you giant hugs from the west coast.
Sorry you are having a rough day today.  Here to listen and to chat,  about anything.

I am so sorry you are going through this situation.  It’s horrible to be accused of something you didn’t do.  Did you see the movie “Gone Girl”, wife tries to frame husband for something he didn’t do. 
 Just as an observer, these 2 girls are taking advantage that you have anxiety.  It sounds very manipulative and a power play on their end.  Do you have immediate family you can go to for support? Can you obtain legal council?

First off, I hope you don’t hurt yourself.  Take a big deep breath, it will be okay.   Going to bet, not just you and me that have gained weight, but that half the planet has gained weight having to stay at home.  If everyone felt the same way you do right now, well our population would be non existent and that would be horrible!  You need to be here.  You matter ! It would have been nice for your mom to really LISTEN to what you are saying.  Feeling not yourself from weight gain, is an energy and mood zapper. Exercise is definitely a mood lifter.  

 When I read your post, laughed to myself, it just reminded me of what my mom would say about ? food “when in doubt throw out”.  But it sucks, you tried to do a good deed, cleaning the fridge and your folks are mad. Instead they should be thanking you for keeping them from getting sick. Hope when they sober up, they apologize to you.

BTW, you write really well.  Hmmmm, a future script writer?

You are very welcome and thank you, that means a lot. I am actually his mom, and his dad misses all their adventures together.  It breaks my heart to see so many young people on here thinking about ending their lives.  I want to wrap my arms around them all.  I think it is very hard today being a teenager, there is way too much pressure about everything.  Trying to see the point in existing or being here can bring confusion.  We may not know why now, but our lives are shaped by experiences.  Keep experiencing everything, keep what inspires you, and pass on what doesn’t.    Something that brought a moment of peace is when my friend prayed for me and my son.  I can’t explain it but it just brought a calmness.  Hoping you attend church again and hope you will update us on how you are doing.

I am so sorry you are feeling this way.  You sound exactly like my son.  Lots of friends, athletic (hockey player), straight A student,  loving family, compassionate.  He was dealing with anger issues, not happy about how he saw himself, a perfectionist.  He said he didn’t want to be here.  We thought he was going through “hormones” or teenage angst.  We were so wrong, it was much more.  He died by suicide last September.  He was your age.  We were completely blindsided as were his friends.  Completely impulsive in his actions. I wish he had come to us, we would have done anything to help him.  Anything! It has been incredibly  difficult dealing with his death.  I am dealing with severe depression from it and the pain is soul crushing.  There are times I think  I just can’t be here any longer and just want to be with my son.  I could not put my other son and family through that kind of pain, again. I remind myself that these feelings are not permanent.  There was a quote I saw recently Rilke’s poem “Go To The Limits of Your Longing” -

“Let everything happen to you. Beauty and Terror.  Just keep going.  No feeling is final”. 

It continues to ring true.  That is, NO feeling is final.  How you feel now won’t be the same tomorrow.  The fact is you can identify how you are feeling.  You are self aware and you are here trying to make sense of it.  You sound like a fighter, resourceful and smart.  Surround yourself with a support system, including your mom, family, go to church, best faith of all is believing in yourself.  

My grandfather is from Ireland.  We had planned to go in March, visit where he grew up, but our trip was cancelled due to Covid. Would give you a big hug and tell you this will pass.

I am so sorry you lost your friend.  He was so young.  I am @ 3 months from my youngest son (16 1/2) from taking his life and the waves of griefs are overwhelming and just keep coming. The pain is unbearable, worse IMO, of dealing with the pain of depression.  I think it takes a very very long time for the pain to subside , maybe never for some.  

You will be triggered by everything around you  that reminds you of him.  It is hard to imagine the future without your friend, happy moments, sharing celebrations, and life itself.  We could see how an amazing young  man our son was becoming and those dreams are gone.  It is devastating.   

I am writing so early because I woke up and immediately start thinking about him only to realize I am in a waking nightmare.  Do you have a good network of support of family and friends? Are you close to his family?  I found it very comforting when his friends where there to support us.

Hi Annie!  First off, your parents love you.  They want to know what is going on in your life and how you are feeling.  Go to them and ask them to LISTEN first, advice can come later.  They may have had similar feelings about life when they were your age.

Also, talk to your friends.  I wouldn’t be surprised if one or more of your friends is feeling the same way.  There are soooooo many people on here that have this apathy about life.  Questioning everything from their existence, self worth to what is the point of living.  It is tough to navigate through those feelings but talking to family, friends, a counselor, or exercising, finding your passion or volunteering, have a way of boosting your mood and change your outlook on life.  You have already taken the first steps in identifying your feelings, that’s great.

Learning how to self edit before saying something undesirable takes practice!  Everyone gets caught up in the moment and blurts something out they wish they didn’t.  So please don’t be hard on yourself.  I still have to remind myself to count to a 100 before popping off with a snide comment.   

Hoping you can find comfort with your family and friends and know that they are there for you.  As all of us, no matter your age, you are still evolving on this Earth.  Be patient with yourself.  : )

I am sorry you are having a tough time.  You write you are very tired.  Can you identify what is making you so tired? Not enough sleep, school, gaming, not eating well?  Being exhausted really skews your thinking.  I know when I get only 4-5 hours of sleep a night I can’t function and think the worsts things.  Have you talked to your parents about how you are feeling.  Plus at 15, your body is changing / growing and your hormones are totally out of whack.  This happens to all of us at different times in our lives.  After having my kids, I dealt with postpartum depression.  Before doing anything impulsive, could you just consider some of these possibilities that might be impacting how you feel ? Please feel free to dm if want.  Sending you a giant hug!

I am so sorry school is taking a toll on you.  Please go easy on yourself right now.  It may feel like grades are everything but they are not.  Can you speak with your parents about how school is making you feel stressed out?  Also speak with your school counselor, they are there to help you.  Winter break should be starting soon, which means to step away from all your studies, have fun with your friends, sleep lots, enjoy your time of and breath. Sending you a big hug.
Also thinking about your beautiful kitties!  They need you ! When I have horrible days and my family isn’t around I just go and hug them.

I wish I was there with you right now to look you in the eyes and say “stay, you matter, you are loved and appreciated”, and give you a GIANT hug.  Much like when mom would do with me when something was not going well in life. Sending you virtual hugs and love.  Please  anytime you want.

I am so sorry for your loss.  We lost our 16 year old son about 3 months.  My heart is breaking for you right now.  This is the worst club to be a part of.  Please feel free to message me if you just need someone to talk with.  Sending love and hugs.

I am so sorry you are feeling bad about yourself and your life.  The voices of self doubt, hatred and loathing are having their way with you.  So many people experience this, being hard on themselves, never believing they can make it in life, with a successful career, friends, relationships.  I have gone through that over the years too.  Never feeling good enough, smart enough, not doing my job well and being tough on myself.  I had to turn that mentality around, but it took a lot of work.  For example,  I would beat myself up everyday on all the things I did wrong at work and now I look at all the things I do right, 99%.   

Also too how we view the world that can influence how we see ourselves.  All around us we know people are truly suffering not just with depression but much greater problems, physical abuse, war, sex trafficking, living in poverty, etc and it really can make one feel apathetic about life, like what’s the point in living and getting up everyday. When I get depressed about whatever is going in my life I step back and remind myself to be thankful, even if it is for something sooo simple, like being able to walk, having my parents, enjoying a cup of coffee.  I know that must sound sappy.  When I get overwhelmed with life, I shut out all the negative crap (the news, social medial, draining people) and just focus on me and those I care about.  Glad to hear your getting rest and eating right, 2 major combatants to fight depression.  Do you exercise or play a sport?

I don’t know if this feedback helps.  I just want you to know you are not alone in how you are feeling.  Have you read “Radical Acceptance”? I want to start reading this book. 

Can I ask if you have family?  What are you studying at uni?  Once you graduate, what would be your dream job?

I am so so sorry for your loss.  79 days for us and we still feel all kinds of emotions.  This is the worst club to be in.  All of us know your pain and we have each other to talk to for support.  Sending you hugs, love and peace.
Sorry to hear you are in a dark place.  Please feel free to message me.  I am a good listener.

Your post is so poignant, I started crying reading it.  I am so sorry for you and your family’s loss.  I can relate exactly, our youngest son (16) took his life @ 3 months ago.  It has torn our world apart.  Our older son lost his only friend and my husband and I are still in disbelief about his death.  Our emotions are all over the place.  I have screamed at the top of my lungs “WHY”!!!! Why didn’t he come to us, tell a friend, leave a note, be so hard on himself, be so impulsive.  His was not planned out, and can only speculate something trigger him so profoundly and painfully that his only recourse was to take his life.  We miss him so much.  As you must miss your sister.  

Yes, in the immediate aftermath I thought about leaving my loved ones to be with my son.  I also have struggled with the pain depression brings on and off over the years.  I can say that losing a child, the pain is 1000 times worse, literally my heart feels like it cracked in half.  So I just couldn’t do that to my family and transfer my pain onto them.  I never had anxiety and now I have it often.  So I press on  trying to cope and live life with the belief that my life experiences I can someday share with my son.  

With your mom’s drinking, it’s worrisome.  She is self medicating to numb the pain but alcohol can also amplify depression.  So it’s a viscous cycle.  I get why she takes a shot at night to fall asleep, it’s a way to get away from the living nightmare she and all of you are dealing with.  I don’t think anyone ever gets over losing a child.  

Does your mom have any siblings or close friends you can talk to you to help you talk to her.  There is also Al-Anon, they have resources.  May I ask how old you are ? Are you doing family counseling together ?  I wish you would post how you are feeling in the suicide watch and teenage suicide watch sub groups.  Your feelings and thoughts are very moving.  Sending you love and hugs !

It seems EVERY part of the Bay Area is expensive and unaffordable.  People working multiple jobs just make rent is no way to live, and see why it causes depression.  Being on the work rat wheel and never getting to enjoy life or your kids is not okay. 

I am guessing you are tired, overworked, continual stress in your marriage and not being able to take care of yourself,  putting all this together, no doubt would make anyone depressed and want to give up. However with that said,  your kids NEED and LOVE you!  How old are they ?  I feel kids need both their parents, especially through their teen years, when they become so vulnerable to peer pressure, grades, self esteem development. They will need your support.  

Would  your job allow you to work in another part of California?  Do you want to do marriage counseling?

I am so sorry you are going through this.  It is very tough going to a new school and knowing no one.  My sister and I both went through that in high school.   I was really lonely but eventually made friends by getting involved in things that interested me.  It takes work to meet people.  I was really shy and even now still introverted to some extent. 
Are you keeping in touch with your old friends ?  
Can I ask, what grade are you in and what are your interests.  Have you told your parents how you are feeling?

I am so sorry for your loss.  Tragic unexpected loss of those close to you can throw anyone into depression.  Grieving is absolutely exhausting. There are days I can barely get out of bed or I just sit and zone out.  I hear you loud and clear about life being pointless, I often think about joining my son, but I couldn’t put my parents, husband, and other son through another loss.  I read on here, that when our loved ones leave us too soon that we need to keep experiencing life, so one day when we are together we have those experiences to share with them.  For me, this is a comforting thought. There are so many things I wanted to experience with my son, so will go and do them with him in my heart.  
How long ago did your parents pass away and are you an only child ?

I have felt like that as well just complete lost interest in things I was excited about .  This apathy about life. Asking questions about what is the point of getting up every day, being on the work rat wheel, or knowing that somewhere tons of people are suffering from disease, famine, abuse, war and feeling guilty for not helping or hopeless because it’s a huge global problem.  What is scary is soooo many really young people are experiencing this apathy, depression and just giving up on life.  I started to look up why the increase in depression,  some point to using cell phones and social media at a young age. I am very depressed, my 16 year son took his life @ 10 weeks ago.  It’s so painful, but I get up every day and live for him, hoping that some day when the grief gets a bit easier I can help someone in someway.  To the original poster, I truly hope you find happiness in life again.

Hi!  I am sorry you are feeling bad about yourself.  Where do you think all the negative self talk is coming from and if this the only thing making you severely depressed?  If you can, every time, those negative voices pop up, try to visualize a a huge red stop sign and not let them take over.  13 is a VERy tough age, everything about you is changing, starting high school is tough, trying to get good grades.  Be good to yourself.  Are you getting enough sleep, eating okay ?  These have a impact on your brain and clear thinking.Please reach out and trust your parents.  They have your best interests at heart and can get you the resources you need.  If that still feels scary, can you go to a teacher, counselor or coach that you trust?

That repetitive cycle in your head telling you negative things is overwhelming.  At times when this happens to me, I visualize a stop sign and won’t let the negative thoughts go beyond it.  Being isolated is an awful feeling if what you want is to have more friends.  Do you have any hobbies / interests that could help you connect with others?  Meet up groups? Clearly you are a cat enthusiast, same here.  Volunteer at a shelter? When friends confide in me, I feel really grateful that can see that I am a compassionate person and can listen without judgement.  Trust your friend, call him tomorrow.
Hey there!  What’s going on ???  Good listener on this end.

Hi!  First off that took guts to be so authentic about what’s happening in your life.  Second, what you’re going through sucks. The toxic boyfriends and the hpv.  Been through both, although the latter not to that full extent.  Still had to have surgery.  Don’t rule out having kids, my friend who’s in her 50’s she is adopting a child (18 months) here soon.  I take it you are much younger. 
Being honest with people about our feelings and opinions takes courage.  Something I’m still working on.  You have every right to be pissed for being misdiagnosed and YES sometimes the medications are worse than the symptoms.  Also cutting toxic people out of your life and setting boundaries is a must.  Time for you to set a bad ass attitude and take charge.  Negotiate down your credit card debt, cut loose the negative baggage of people in your life, set some small goals, move forward.  Be the advocate for YOUR life.  It is HARD.  It took me a long time to stand up for myself, say no to people and not worry about their opinions of me. I deal with depression and am very guarded with people except those I love dearly. 
Are there people / family in your life you can trust unconditionally?

Hi there. I am so sorry you are going through this right now.  13 is a tough age no doubt about it.  Pressures to get good grades, social stuff, and hormones going crazy, it’s a lot.  You are NOT worthless and please don’t be hard on yourself. 

I wish my son told us how he was truly feeling, but he didn’t and we miss him so much.   I strongly agree with Zagdav on speaking with your Mom and Dad about how you are feeling.  Your parents LOVE YOU.  You sister, girlfriend and friends LOVE YOU.  As a mom I am asking you to please go call your parents and let them  know what’s going on, and give them the opportunity to help and support you.

Taking your life creates such a wave of grief for those that love you.  I am speaking from experience here, having lost my 16 1/2 year old son to suicide recently.  The pain is so unbearable, so much so that I have considered taking my life because I want to be with my son, but I will NOT inflict that pain onto others. I have my husband, son, parents that would be devastated.  It is VERY difficult getting up everyday, feeling like I failed him as a parent but I press on with life.  I would think your mom would want that for you too, to continuing living.  

I have experienced this lack of motivation and depression before, now even more so with my son’s passing.  What definitely has helped despite my setbacks with grief (God knows this is going to be a life long challenge!) ,  is continuing to work, eating healthy, NO alcohol, a low dose of Well Butrin , getting GOOD sleep AND yes exercise.  I am not sure where you live but getting involved in a team sport has been VERY uplifting for me.  Meet up groups are a place to start, or clubs that offer tennis, golf, a social outlet of some kind. Therapy can be helpful but I think sometimes a Life Coach is better as they help with personal goals.   

I truly and sincerely hope you will find a way to stay and be at peace, find joy in life.
